howto.name: Choose a recording or video
howto.text: Drop or choose a speech recording, or a video whose sound you want cleaned. MP3, WAV, M4A, MP4, MOV, WebM and MKV files are read a minute at a time, up to 60 minutes of sound; OGG, Opus, FLAC and AAC files, and MP4s written in fragments, are decoded whole, up to 15 minutes. The file is read in this browser and is not uploaded.

howto.name: Set the strength
howto.text: At 100%, the default, you get only the cleaned sound. If the voice comes out thin or watery, lower it: at 70%, for example, three tenths of your original, noise included, is mixed back in.

howto.name: Remove the noise
howto.text: Click Remove noise. RNNoise, an open-source noise suppressor, cleans each channel on your device; it comes from this site, about 3 MB, the first time. The bar shows how far it has got and the time left at the speed so far. Keep the tab open.

howto.name: Compare and download
howto.text: Play the original and the cleaned sound, the pauses especially, then click Download WAV. The file is named after yours, such as interview-clean.wav: 16-bit, at 48 kHz, mono or stereo as your recording was. To change the strength, go back and clean it again.

faq.q: How do I remove background noise from audio for free?
faq.a: Choose the recording here and click Remove noise. It is free, with no account, no watermark and no limit on how many recordings you clean. Everything happens in your browser: RNNoise listens to the sound in frames of 10 milliseconds, keeps what it hears as a voice and turns the rest down. Then compare the result with the original and download the WAV.

No. The file is read and cleaned in your browser, and it is not sent to PrivaTools or anyone else. The only download is the noise remover itself, about 3 MB of WebAssembly from this site, the first time you clean a recording; your browser keeps it. Unless you turn analytics off on the Privacy page, Google Analytics receives an event saying the tool was used and whether it worked, never the sound.

Not well. RNNoise was trained to keep speech and remove everything else, so it treats instruments as noise: a song comes out quieter, thinner or damaged, and music under a voice is turned down with the noise. It also doesn't separate one voice from another, and it doesn't remove echo or the reverberation of a room.

Steady noise under a voice: mains hum, a fan or air conditioner, traffic, the hiss of a room or of a cheap microphone. Sudden sounds such as a door, a dog or typing are reduced less reliably, and other people talking stay, because they are speech too. In our tests on synthetic speech with white or pink noise added 5 dB below it, full strength turned the noise in the pauses down by 31 to 38 dB.

faq.q: Is it the same as an AI voice enhancer?
faq.a: No. It suppresses noise: what you hear is your own recording with the noise turned down, and nothing is added that wasn't there. Some AI enhancers recreate the voice itself, which can sound like a studio recording but can also change words or the voice. Here, very loud noise can leave traces and very quiet speech can come out thinner; lowering the strength keeps more of the original.

Audio: MP3, WAV, M4A and AAC, OGG and Opus, FLAC and WebM. Video: the sound of MP4, MOV, M4V, WebM and MKV files; only the cleaned sound comes back, as a WAV, to put back with the picture in a video editor. The browser has to decode the sound itself. When it can't, because of an unusual codec or a damaged file, the tool says so and nothing is sent anywhere: Extract Audio, for a video, and Audio Converter, for a recording, can make an MP3 of it on the PrivaTools server, which means uploading the file, up to 500 MB, for temporary processing; the MP3 then works here.

faq.q: How long can the recording be?
faq.a: Up to 60 minutes of sound. MP3, WAV, M4A, MP4, MOV, WebM and MKV files are read and cleaned a minute at a time, so a long file needs little more memory than a short one; OGG, Opus, FLAC and AAC files, and MP4s written in fragments, are decoded whole, up to 15 minutes. RNNoise runs on your own processor: on a two-core test computer it took about 10 seconds for each minute of mono sound, and twice that for stereo. Most laptops are faster and phones slower. To clean a longer recording, cut it into parts first.

faq.q: Why is the result a WAV at 48 kHz?
faq.a: WAV holds the sound uncompressed, so cleaning doesn't add a second round of compression, and every editor and player opens it. RNNoise works at 48 kHz, so the result comes at that rate, 16-bit, mono or stereo as your recording was. WAV files are large, about 5.8 MB a minute in mono and 11.5 MB in stereo: Audio Converter can turn one into an MP3, which means uploading it to PrivaTools for temporary processing.

faq.q: What does the strength setting do?
faq.a: It mixes the cleaned sound with your original. At 100% you hear only the cleaned sound; at 70%, seven tenths of it with three tenths of the original, noise included. Mixing some of the original back in hides the traces heavy cleaning can leave, at the cost of some noise: at 90%, the noise can be at most about 20 dB quieter than it was.
